title: Scanned
description:
What a scan the panel asked for found ([`Query::Scan`]): what `flayer
scan --suggest --json` prints, each directory with what the panel needs
to offer it, and what the command warns of beside it.

A shape of the backend's rather than the envelope the command prints,
since what it adds to each directory is a front end's: the words the
command says why in, what marking it asks for, and the entry a relink
names. Each worked out here, in Rust, where the minds screen works out
the same, rather than by the panel from the scan's fields.

depth.description: How many levels below each root it looked.

found.description:
Every directory it found, in the order `flayer scan --suggest` ranks
them: what is not linked first, most worth linking first, then what
is.

roots.description:
Where it looked, each once, in the order given: the workspace's root
when it was given none.

truncated.description:
Whether it stopped at core's bound before looking everywhere, which
`warnings` says too.

untraced.description:
Each entry where no project is any more whose id the ledger never
learned, as the scan spells it: what `flayer relink <entry> <path>`
follows, which only somebody who knows where it went can type.

warnings.description:
What it could not read, and that it stopped early, as `flayer scan`
warns of them, each with its code.

Found.description:
A directory a workspace could manage.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name. The panel reads it in what a scan it asks for is answered
with, so it says its TypeScript too.

agent_files.description:
Each name at its root an agent reads something from
([`Agent::reads_at_root`], of every agent), in name order: what makes
a repository's reason [`Reason::Agents`], and listed for a mind
project too, which can hold them as well. Looked at, never followed
or read: a link there counts as what it is called.

id.description:
The id its settings name it by (D-09), whatever it is called and
wherever it is: none for a git repository that is not a project yet,
for a project a `mind.toml` still marks, which has none, and for one
whose marker would not open, which is a failure beside it.

linked.description: Whether the workspace links it already.

mind.description:
A mind project already, rather than a git repository that is not one
yet and would need `mind init` before it can be linked.

moved.description:
The entry it moved from, when it is not linked and holds the id the
workspace's ledger last saw at an entry where no project is any more
([`MindProject::is_vacant`]): spelled as `route` is, so `flayer
relink <moved> <route>` run there follows it. None otherwise, and for
an id another directory holds too, which is a copy rather than a
move.

reason.description: Why it is worth linking: the strongest of what it holds.

route.description:
What `flayer link` would be given for it, run where the request
spells routes from: the route from there, `/` separated, when it is
inside, and its path otherwise.

MindsChange.description:
What one directory's mark on the minds screen asks of the workspace, when
it differs from how the directory started: what [`Task::minds`] is built
from. By its name in snake_case in JSON: `"init_and_link"`.

oneOf.description:
`mind init` in it, then link it: a repository that is not a mind
project yet.

ProjectId.description: A project's id: 128 random bits, written as 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

ScanReason.description:
Why a directory a scan found is worth linking, the strongest of what
it holds, best first: a mind project its settings name by an id, one
with none, a git repository an agent reads something in, and any
other git repository.

Suggestion.description: One directory a scan found, and what the panel offers for it.

moved_from.description:
The entry it moved from, as the marker spells it, which a relink
names: matched by core's `scan::moved_from`, as the minds screen
matches it, since the scan spells `moved` as `flayer link` would
take it. None when it did not move.

offers.description:
What marking it asks for ([`MindsChange::of_found`]): linking it, or
making it a project first. None for one linked, and for one found
moved, which wants a relink rather than a second entry beside the one
it left stale.

why.description:
Why it is worth linking, in the words `flayer scan --suggest` and the
minds screen say it in ([`worth_linking`]); none for one linked.

Warning.description:
One line a command says beside what it reports, on stderr: a warning, a
note, a hint, or an error about one part of what it did; and the code of
what it says, when what it says has one.

The text is what a terminal shows, word for word, `warning: ` and all.
The code rides beside it for the panel, which acts on a condition by its
code rather than by matching English that is reworded whenever it is
made clearer: the code core gives what went wrong ([`mindweaver_core::code`]),
or the CLI's own ([`CliError::code`]). A line with none says something no
code is given to: a hint, a note, or what the CLI makes of what it found
rather than something that went wrong. Kept beside the text rather than
in a list of its own beside the lines, which every line pushed would have
to keep in step with.

Serialized as it is, `{"text": ..., "code": ...}`, in what a run of the
panel's backend says (`backend::Run`): the line a terminal shows, and
the code beside it.
